title: When the Fitting ideal of a bounded complex with respect to a nonzerodivisor is principal, the shifted complex is locally free and its differential splits off

standard_prerequisites.name: The Fitting ideal I_i(M, f) is generated by the r_i by r_i minors of the map (f, d^i) and its powers of f vanish after localizing at f
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the generator g and lets the author read the rank of the map after localizing, which gives the vanishing of the higher minors.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module whose Fitting invariant is principal and which is defined by the minors of a map is finite locally free of the corresponding rank, and a finite projective module over a local ring is free
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the quotient Q is finite locally free of rank r_{i+1} and f-torsion free, which identifies the cokernel modulo f-power torsion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The shifted complex eta_f M has as its i-th term the kernel of the map (d^i, -1) from f^i M^i direct sum f^{i+1} M^{i+1} to f^i M^{i+1}
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the term of the shifted complex with the kernel in question and thereby with a direct summand of the finite free module.

core_obligations: Choose a generator g of the principal Fitting ideal I_i(M, f) and note that g divides a power of f because f^{r_i} lies in that ideal, so that g is a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 28060-28062).

Record that the r_i by r_i minors of the map (f, d^i) generate the Fitting ideal and that the (r_i + 1) by (r_i + 1) minors vanish, the latter checked after localizing at f where the rank of the map is r_i (proof lines 28063-28068).

Consider the surjection onto the quotient of the cokernel of (f, d^i) by its g-torsion, apply the fitting ideal statement to see that this quotient is finite locally free of rank r_{i+1}, conclude that it is f-torsion free and hence that the cokernel modulo f-power torsion is that quotient (proof lines 28069-28078).

Consider the displayed complex of finite free modules, note that it becomes split exact after localizing at f, identify its middle map with the map (f, d^i) studied above, and conclude that the image Q' of the right hand map is isomorphic to Q and in particular projective (proof lines 28080-28093).

Use the construction of the shifted complex to see that the image of the injective map (1, d^i) is the kernel of (d^i, -1), hence that the i-th term of the shifted complex is a direct summand of the finite free module f^i M^i direct sum f^{i+1} M^{i+1}, which gives both conclusions (proof lines 28094-28101).
proof_roadmap: Take a generator of the principal Fitting ideal and record its divisibility by a power of f (proof lines 28060-28062).
Read off the ranks from the minors after localizing at f and form the quotient by g-torsion, which is finite locally free of the next rank (proof lines 28063-28078).
Show that the displayed complex of finite free modules is split exact after inverting f and identify the image of its right hand map with a projective module (proof lines 28080-28093).
Identify the shifted term with the kernel of the second map and read off local freeness of the right rank and the splitting (proof lines 28094-28101).
difficulty_reason: The statement assumes that the Fitting ideal I_i(M, f) attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules and a nonzerodivisor is principal, and concludes that the shifted complex is locally free with explicit ranks and that its differential is the inclusion of a direct summand (statement lines 28049-28057). The proof works with the minors of the map (f, d^i): after localizing at f the rank is r_i, so the higher minors vanish, which makes the quotient by g-torsion finite locally free and f-torsion free, and the displayed complex of finite free modules is then used to identify the image of the second map with a projective module, after which the shifted term is recognised as a direct summand (proof lines 28059-28101). The subtle step is the passage from the cokernel to the cokernel modulo f-power torsion, which is what makes the projective module appear. The counted span refers twice, once to a fitting ideal statement of this chapter and once to the section in which the shifted complex is constructed, both carried as navigation stubs.
